newsitem.title: HONDURAS: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

HONDURAS, April 28 - Puerto Cortes - Vessels berthed, 4 discharging/loading containers, 1 each discharging corn, sbm. 4 Vessels awaiting berth to discharge/load containers. Vessels due, 5 to discharge bananas, 1 passenger vessel, 3 to load/discharge containers. Labour day 1/5. Four vessels berthed of which 2 discharging/loading containers/generals, 1 discharging fertiliser, 1 discharging wheat, 1 anchored in ballast. 24 Vessels due of which 1 passenger, 14 to discharge/load containers/general, 6 to discharge/load containers/bananas, 1 to load lumber, 1 to discharge fuel oil. Dredging continues in order to try to maintain 30 ft. alongside.

PANAMA, April 27 - Cristobal - 14 Vessels alongside of which 5 operating. Balboa - 18 Vessels alongside, 1 operating. Panama Canal Authorities removed sunken tug and now transiting vessels to their utmost capacity. Advise projected backlogs at 0001 hrs 28/4, 89 vessels, 24 hrs, 99 vessels, 48 hours, 85 vessels. Delays approx. 3 days for all vessels arriving 27/4. Due to expected heavy arrivals, may be 10 days or more before backlog reduced to normal levels. Booking system now in condition 2. Authorities expected to invoke condition 3 at 0001 on 29/4, for rest of week. Report received on 29/4 stated that from 2400 hrs 1/5, projected backlog of vessels 81. Non-booked panamax/restricted vessels being delayed 3-4 days, small vessels 2 days.

UNITED STATES, April 28 - Honolulu, HI - Harbour - 4 Tugs and barges alongside. Barbers Point - Harbour - 2 Barges alongside. Offport mooring - 1 Tanker. Hampton Roads, VA - Four general cargo/container vessels in pier operating, 4 bulkers in pier loading coal, 5 anchored waiting to load. 1 Bulker loading fertiliser, 1 discharging cement, 1 loading scrap. 5 Vessels in pier under repair/layberth. Baltimore, MD - Vessels operating, 6 bulkers, 3 container vessels, 2 ro-ro, 1 auto vessel, 1 tanker, 3 general cargo, 2 cable vessels on standby. 4 Vessels in repair yard, 3 bulkers awaiting berth. Jersey city, Port Elizabeth, Perth Amboy, Bayway, Cartaret, NJ - One vessel in each port. Port Newark, NJ - Three vessels in port.

EAST COAST - Baltimore, MD - Dundalk terminal - No congestion expected this week. Clear C.D canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators, coal operations and liquid bulk facilities working well with no delays. Consol coal - 2 Days average waiting time. Anchorage available at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC. - Expansion of the Columbus street terminal interchange facility approved by the south Carolina state port authority. This will help to reduce delays within the terminal. Delays to vessel operations expected during next week. Miami, FL - Port of Miami and port Everglades working normally this week, traffic expected to be moderate. New York, NY - No congestion at anchorages, container or tanker terminals. Sugar terminals congested.

Norfolk, VA - Southern Coal pier - 12 Vessels due during this week, 6 anchored waiting to load at present. Dominion terminal - 8 Vessels due. Pier IX terminal - 5 Vessels due during the next week. Scheduled maintenance to no.1 ship loader at Norfolk Southern Coal pier no.6 completed 23.00 hrs. 25/4. Cargill - No vessels due during the coming week. Container and general cargo terminals working normally with no delays. Oil and bulk terminals all working normally. All channels open, with prevailing depths available. Philadelphia, PA - No congestion at Philadelphia, Camden or Wilmington. No dredging/repairs or navigational problems.

Savannah, GA - Garden City terminals - Expect a moderate week with the heaviest congestion on Wednesday. Ocean terminals - Expect a moderate week throughout the entire period. East coast terminal - Expects a moderate week with no delays. Colonial Marine terminals bulk clay facility - Expects long delays. Savannah - Sugar refinery has only one barge scheduled for Monday. All bulk liquid facilities working normally, with no congestion expected. Navigational conditions normal. As the weather warms, afternoon thunderstorms may cause some downtime on weather-sensitive cargoes.

GULF COAST - Houston, TX - No congestion at the port of Houston city docks, Cargill grain elevator or Houston public grain elevator. However, congestion exists in some private terminals for break bulk cargo such as Greensport and Manchester terminal and some oil/chemical terminals. New Orleans, LA - Seasonal rain may cause delays in cargo operation, especially grain loading. Grain shipments normal for this season. River stage at 14.0 feet. Expect to go down to 13.5 ft. by 28/4. Normal transit times can be expected. Bar pilots advise that the draft for the Mississippi river gulf outlet will be 36 ft. Spillway to be closed by 18/4. Based on these drafts, vessels are advised to maintain sufficient airdraft for transit under bridges in Mississippi river. High river conditions will cause delays in ship movement and vessel transit times. Present max. permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 44 ft. Fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt, 43 ft. Fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt.

WEST COAST - Columbia river - At present there are 6 grain vessels in the Columbia river district, 4 loading at berth and 2 waiting at anchorage locations. Average waiting period 1-3 days at most facilities. Coos Bay, OR - Past week slow. Only 1 wood-chip carrier loading and 1 vessel discharging nickel at Glenbrook terminal. Next week also appears to be somewhat slow with most activity centred at Roseburg dock with 3 arrivals scheduled for the end of April. Another nickel vessel is due at Glenbrook midweek.

Honolulu, HI - Midway island has officially been transferred from the U.S. navy to the U.S. park service. Midway Phoenix Corp. is now running the small hospital, tugboat and air service on the island. The effect of this change for mariners is that marine medical evacuations will be handled through a commercial company rather than the U.S. military, at a substantial increase to the ship companies/p.i clubs. The inland boatmen's union has set up a picket line at the Entrancto Smith Maritime's Uaukewai diving company. The union has won a representational election at the company, but management refuses to bargain. Gale warnings are in effect for Hawaiian waters with predicted winds of 30-40 knots and seas 18-20 ft. Harbour pilots advise that additional tugs may be needed for mooring in these conditions. Off port bunkering conditions will be marginal during the upcoming week.

Long beach, CA - Metropolitan (lb-212-216) looks moderate for April/May at present, with 1-2 days at anchor awaiting berth expected. Koch Carbon (lb-211) - at present, the months of April and May appear light. Kaiser (lr-49) - At present looks moderately quiet for April/May. (Coal/petcoke) - Anticipate no delays waiting on berth. Bulk cargoes - At present, April/May looks moderate for Los Angeles/Long Beach harbour for bulk cargoes.
